h1: The 6 Best 85 Inch TVs for Big Living Rooms and Home Theaters, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best 80 to 85 Inch TVs 2026: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 6 TVs at 85 inches from Samsung, Hisense and Insignia, compared on panel type, Mini-LED, refresh rate, smart platform and value.
summary: The Samsung M80H Mini-LED is the 85 inch TV to buy for a big room, pairing a Mini-LED backlight with Samsung's smart platform. The Hisense 85 inch U7 is the gaming pick at 165Hz, the Samsung Q8F is the QLED all-rounder from 2025, and the Insignia F50 is the Fire TV option that keeps the price lowest among the brand-name sets.
intro: At 85 inches, a TV stops being an appliance and becomes a piece of the room. That changes what to look for. Viewing distance matters, since you want to sit about nine or ten feet back, and so does the panel technology, because a screen this large magnifies any weakness in black levels, uniformity and motion. Spec-sheet features that are hard to see on a 55 inch set become obvious on an 85.

We ranked six sets at or near 85 inches across three families: Samsung's Crystal UHD, QLED and Mini-LED lines, Hisense's U7, and Insignia's Fire TV. The listings give us panel type, refresh rate and smart platform but rarely brightness or dimming zones, so the ranking follows technology class. A seventh candidate, a 75 inch model, was left out because it falls below the size range.

products.name: Samsung 85-Inch Class M80H Series
products.verdict: Samsung's Mini-LED technology at 85 inches, the strongest panel class in the group.
products.description:
The M80H is an 85 inch Samsung with a Mini-LED backlight. Mini-LED uses a dense grid of small LEDs behind the panel that can be dimmed in zones, which gives deeper blacks and stronger highlights than a plain LED backlight.

The M80H takes top place because panel quality matters most at this size. On a screen 85 inches wide, haloing around bright objects and grey blacks are far more visible, and local dimming through Mini-LED is the best way to fight both. It also benefits from Samsung's smart platform and long software support. The listing does not mention refresh rate, so gamers should check before ordering.

Buy it for a dedicated home theater or a large living room. The price tier is not stated in the data we reviewed.
products.idealFor: Home theaters and big living rooms that watch films.
products.skipIf: You need a confirmed high refresh rate.

products.name: Hisense 85" U7 Mini-LED ULED 4K UHD Best Premium Gaming Smart Google
products.verdict: An 85 inch Mini-LED with a 165Hz refresh rate, aimed squarely at gamers.
products.description:
The Hisense U7 is an 85 inch Mini-LED set with a 165Hz refresh rate and Google's smart platform. It is priced at $500 and up, and the listing frames it as a premium gaming TV.

It is second because it combines the same Mini-LED technology as the Samsung with a refresh rate that few big TVs offer. 165Hz suits fast PC and console play, and motion looks smoother on a very large screen. Samsung wins on ecosystem polish and long-term support, which is why the M80H stays ahead.

Buy it if you game on a console or PC and want a giant screen. A user who only watches films may not need the extra refresh rate.
products.idealFor: Gamers who want a giant, fast screen.
products.skipIf: You do not game and want the longest support.

products.name: Samsung 85-Inch Class QLED Q8F 4K UHD Smart TV (2025 Model) Q4 AI
products.verdict: A 2025 QLED with Q4 AI processing, built for demanding, frequent use.
products.description:
The Q8F is an 85 inch Samsung QLED, a 2025 model with Q4 AI processing and 4K resolution, priced at $500 and up. QLED adds a quantum dot layer for rich colour.

It ranks third because QLED is a step below Mini-LED for contrast, but it brings strong colour and brightness at a more conventional price. AI processing upscales lower-resolution content, which is valuable at 85 inches where cable and streaming sources look soft. The newer processor also helps with smart features.

Buy it for a living room that mixes sports, streaming and movies. If contrast is your priority, step up to the Mini-LED.
products.idealFor: Mixed viewing of sports, streaming and films.
products.skipIf: Black levels are your top priority.

products.name: Samsung 85-Inch Class QN70H Series
products.verdict: An 85 inch QLED from Samsung's QN70H line, priced at $500 and up.
products.description:
The QN70H is an 85 inch Samsung QLED. The listing gives little beyond the size and panel type, and it sits at $500 and up.

It ranks fourth because QLED is a safe, proven panel type but the data gives us nothing to separate it from the Q8F, which lists a 2025 model year and processor. Without a refresh rate or processing detail, the Q8F is the better documented purchase. The QN70H still benefits from Samsung's reliability and support.

Buy it if you find it at a sharp price and prefer the Samsung ecosystem. Check the retailer page for refresh rate and processing.
cons: Hard to separate from the Q8F
products.idealFor: Samsung loyalists who find it at a good price.
products.skipIf: You want documented refresh rate and processing.

products.name: INSIGNIA 85" Class F50 Series LED 4K UHD Smart Fire TV with Alexa
products.verdict: An 85 inch LED Fire TV with Alexa, the budget-minded smart choice.
products.description:
The Insignia F50 is an 85 inch LED 4K smart TV with Fire TV built in and Alexa voice control, priced at $500 and up. It is an edge or direct-lit LED design, not Mini-LED or QLED.

It lands fifth because a conventional LED panel cannot match the contrast or colour of the Samsung and Hisense sets above. What it offers is an easy Fire TV interface and voice control through Alexa, which suits households already in Amazon's ecosystem. At 85 inches, the plainer panel shows its limits in dark rooms.

Buy it for a bright living room where convenience matters. Choose a Mini-LED for a movie room.
pros: Fire TV with Alexa built in
products.skipIf: You watch films in a dark room.

products.name: Samsung 85-Inch Class U8000H Series Crystal UHD
products.verdict: Samsung's entry Crystal UHD at 85 inches, a middle-ground price for the feature set.
products.description:
The U8000H is an 85 inch Samsung Crystal UHD 4K TV, priced at $500 and up. Crystal UHD is Samsung's entry LED class, below QLED and Mini-LED.

It finishes last because the panel technology is the plainest in the group, and at 85 inches that shows in contrast and colour compared with QLED. It does give you Samsung's platform and a big picture at the lowest tier of the brand. For casual viewing of shows and news, it is perfectly fine.

Buy it if your priority is the largest screen for the least money from a mainstream brand. Step up to a QLED if film quality matters.
products.idealFor: Casual viewers who want a giant, simple screen.

methodology.title: Panel technology
methodology.description: We ranked Mini-LED above QLED and QLED above plain LED and Crystal UHD, since panel class matters more as screens grow.

methodology.title: Refresh rate
methodology.description: Where listings state refresh rates, such as 165Hz, we credited them for gaming and fast motion on a large screen.

methodology.title: Processing and platform
methodology.description: Smart platforms, AI upscaling and recent model years were weighed for long-term use and for making lower-resolution video look good.

methodology.title: Listing clarity
methodology.description: Sets that document panel type and key features outranked those with only a size and a brand.

methodology.title: Value at 85 inches
methodology.description: Price tiers were weighed against panel class, so a plain LED set only ranks well if it undercuts better technology.

whatMatters.detail: Crystal UHD and basic LED backlights are the plainest, QLED adds a quantum dot layer for colour and brightness, and Mini-LED adds many small zones for contrast. At 85 inches, flaws in black levels are very visible. Check the listing for QLED or Mini-LED in the name.
An 85 inch screen is best viewed from about nine to eleven feet. Closer and you see pixels and have to move your eyes; farther and the size benefit shrinks. Measure your sofa distance before you buy.

A 120Hz or 165Hz panel redraws more times per second, which smooths motion in sports and games. Gamers should look for the stated rate and for HDMI 2.1 ports. A listing without a refresh rate usually means 60Hz.

Most cable and streaming content is below 4K, and an 85 inch screen magnifies softness. AI upscaling processors help clean it up. A newer processor, such as Samsung's Q4 AI, also improves smart features.
An 85 inch TV is heavy and wide, often needing two people to lift it. Check the width against your stand and the VESA pattern against your mount. Plan the delivery path through doors and stairs.

howToChoose.intro: Panel class matters most at this size, so decide how much contrast and brightness you want before comparing smart features.

cards.label: Mini-LED
cards.text: Many small LEDs behind the panel, dimmed in zones for deeper blacks and stronger highlights. The Samsung M80H and Hisense U7 use it.

cards.label: QLED
cards.text: A quantum dot layer improves colour and brightness. The Samsung Q8F and QN70H use it, and they cost less than Mini-LED sets.

howToChoose.note: Choose Mini-LED for dark rooms and films, and QLED for mixed daytime viewing at a lower cost.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Mini-LED or QLED, good black levels, a processor that upscales well and a seating distance around ten feet. Control room light with curtains.

cards.label: In this ranking
cards.text: The Samsung M80H is the best home theater pick, and the Hisense U7 is the alternative if you also game on the same screen.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You watch films in a dark room or game. The Samsung M80H and Hisense U7 bring Mini-LED contrast that shows at 85 inches.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: The TV is for daytime viewing. The Insignia F50 or Samsung U8000H give you the size without Mini-LED.

faq.q: Will an 85 inch TV fit my room?
faq.a: It needs a wall about 75 inches wide and a sofa roughly nine to eleven feet away. Measure the wall, the stand and the delivery path. A smaller TV is better in a small room.

faq.q: What is the common mistake with giant TVs?
faq.a: Buying size over panel quality. A plain LED panel at 85 inches shows grey blacks and weak contrast. Spend a bit more for QLED or Mini-LED.

faq.q: Is Mini-LED worth it over QLED?
faq.a: In a dark room, yes, because local dimming gives deeper blacks. In a bright living room, QLED is often enough. The Samsung Q8F is a good QLED option.

faq.q: How do I mount an 85 inch TV?
faq.a: Use a mount rated above the TV's weight, fix it to wall studs and have a second person help. Check the VESA pattern. A stand with a wide base is an alternative.
Almost certainly. Slim TV speakers are weak, and a big screen deserves better audio. A soundbar with a subwoofer is the usual upgrade.

faq.q: Does the Fire TV Insignia need an Amazon account?
faq.a: Yes. Fire TV requires an Amazon account to download apps and use Alexa features. Prepare your login before setup.

finalTake: The Samsung M80H is the best 85 inch TV in this ranking, with Mini-LED contrast on a big screen. The Hisense U7 is the pick for gamers, and the Samsung Q8F gives strong colour at a lower cost. Choose the Insignia F50 or the Samsung U8000H only if price and size matter more than panel quality.
